difficultyReason: Paradox: correlation (optional-headlights users are safer) doesn't imply causation (mandating headlights reduces collisions). Resolution requires spotting the self-selection confound.
stimulus: In jurisdictions where use of headlights is optional when visibility is good, drivers who use headlights at all times are less likely to be involved in a collision than are drivers who use headlights only when visibility is poor. Yet Highway Safety Department records show that making use of headlights mandatory at all times does nothing to reduce the overall number of collisions.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to resolve the apparent discrepancy in the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: In jurisdictions where use of headlights is optional when visibility is good, one driver in four uses headlights for daytime driving in good weather.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A law making use of headlights mandatory at all times is not especially difficult to enforce.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only very careful drivers use headlights when their use is not legally required.

choices.label: D
choices.text: There are some jurisdictions in which it is illegal to use headlights when visibility is good.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The jurisdictions where use of headlights is mandatory at all times are those where daytime visibility is frequently poor.

explanations.correct: If only very careful drivers voluntarily use headlights, then their lower collision rate reflects their carefulness, not the headlights. Mandating headlights doesn't make reckless drivers careful, so overall collisions don't drop. This dissolves the paradox.
explanations.A: Frequency of voluntary use doesn't by itself explain why mandatory use fails to help.
explanations.B: Enforcement difficulty is not the discrepancy.
explanations.D: Edge-case legal quirk; doesn't explain the overall data.
explanations.E: If anything this would make mandatory headlights more useful, worsening the paradox.

source.notes: Verbatim from LSAC public LR sample page. Correct answer C confirmed.
